id: Practice Direction 41B – Periodical Payments Under The Damages Act 1996
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 41B – PERIODICAL PAYMENTS UNDER THE DAMAGES ACT 1996

# This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Factors to be taken into account (rule 41.7)

## 1.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] The factors which the court shall have regard to under rule 41.7 include –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] (1) the scale of the annual payments taking into account any deduction for contributory negligence;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] (2) the form of award preferred by the claimant including –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] (a) the reasons for the claimant’s preference; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] (b) the nature of any financial advice received by the claimant when considering the form of award; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 1.] (3) the form of award preferred by the defendant including the reasons for the defendant’s preference.

## The award (rule 41.8)

## 2.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.1] An order may be made under rule 41.8(2) where a dependant would have had a claim under section 1 of the Fatal Accidents Act 1976 if the claimant had died at the time of the accident.

## 2.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] Examples of circumstances which might lead the court to order an increase or decrease under rule 41.8(3) are where the court determines that –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] (1) the claimant’s condition will change leading to an increase or reduction in his or her need to incur care, medical or other recurring or capital costs;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] (2) gratuitous carers will no longer continue to provide care;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] (3) the claimant’s educational circumstances will change;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] (4) the claimant would have received a promotional increase in pay;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 2.2] (5) the claimant will cease earning.

## Continuity of payment (rule 41.9)

## 3.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 3.] Before ordering an alternative method of funding under rule 41.9(1), the court must be satisfied that the following criteria are met –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 3.] (1) that a method of funding provided for under section 2(4) of the 1996 Act is not possible or there are good reasons to justify an alternative method of funding;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 3.] (2) that the proposed method of funding can be maintained for the duration of the award or for the proposed duration of the method of funding; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 3.] (3) that the proposed method of funding will meet the level of payment ordered by the court.

## Assignment or charge (rule 41.10)

## 4.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 4.] The factors which the court shall have regard to under rule 41.10 include –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 4.] (1) whether the capitalised value of the assignment or charge represents value for money;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 4.] (2) whether the assignment or charge is in the claimant’s best interests, taking into account whether these interests can be met in some other way; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 4.] (3) how the claimant will be financially supported following the assignment or charge.

## Variation

## 5.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 5.] The Damages (Variation of Periodical Payments) Order 2005 sets out provisions which enable the court in certain circumstances to provide in an order for periodical payments that it may be varied.

## Settlement

## 6.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 6.] Where the parties settle a claim to which rule 36.5 applies, any consent order, whether made under rule 40.6 or on an application under Part 23, must satisfy the requirements of rules 41.8 and 41.9.

## Settlement or compromise on behalf of child or protected party

## 7.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 41 > 7.] Where a claim for damages for personal injury is made by or on behalf of a child or protected party and is settled prior to the start of proceedings or before trial, the provisions of rule 21.10 must be complied with.
